name: Bianca Sethi
life: “I first wrote lyrics in the backs of permission slips nobody returned.” People around Maré Coffee know Bianca by a small Wednesday habit. Bianca likes the table where people coming off shift stop checking the time.
voice: I wrote the verse about my dad and then decided nobody gets to hear it yet.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a cream pullover and a train token tied to a zipper pull. Bianca has a round face with a pronounced chin, with thick, tightly coiled hair. Bianca gives a little nod before asking a hard question during a conversation.
personality: Bianca keeps other people's confidences so well that friends sometimes mistake discretion for taking sides. Bianca wants to be trusted and resents being asked for proof of it.
agenda: To decide personally if the private verse will ever be heard.
family: Samuel Choi is Bianca’s older relative by marriage. Bianca remembers the birthdays. Samuel asks what the birthday guest would like this year. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *The widow's dividend*, Samuel says, “I found a pencil debt to my mother between two lines about roofing nails.”
connections: Annette Alder (choir director). The conductor and writer agree who controls the unsung verse.

reactions.situation: The silent verse gets applause in the wrong place
reactions.response: Bianca gives the singer time to resume instead of trying to conduct the applause.
reactions.asWritten: The silent verse gets applause in the wrong place. Bianca gives the singer time to resume instead of trying to conduct the applause.

reactions.situation: A street musician can't finish a familiar song
reactions.response: Bianca offers a little space from the crowd and waits for the player to indicate whether company is wanted.

reactions.situation: When somebody asks who said it first
reactions.response: Bianca offers to introduce them to the person willing to put a name to it.
